title: Classmates
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: This entry is Sotsugyousei (Graduates), the two-volume continuation of Asumiko Nakamura's Classmates. Studious Rihito Sajou and free-spirited musician Hikaru Kusakabe, a couple from an all-boys high school, face graduation, Sajou's Kyoto University plans and Kusakabe's music dream, and the prospect of a long-distance relationship (MangaUpdates; DMG blurb via AniList; Wikipedia).
life_message: Love that is honest and patient can carry two very different people through growing up and apart geographically.

content.note: Exam stress and uncertainty about the future (MU; Wikipedia).
Same-sex teen romance with 'intimate affection' (MU); MangaDex suggestive; volume 1 reviews say at most French kissing (ANN) (to verify for this sequel).
Sajou's acute anxiety and panic attacks (Wikipedia; MU Insecure Character).

dominant: First love between two boys; graduation and diverging paths; acceptance

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts are talked through; no face-saving fights (ANN on vol. 1).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Kusakabe's free spirit clashes with Sajou's propriety (DMG blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friends and a teacher mentor matter more than family (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Equal partners; teacher Hara acts as an informal mentor (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Choices of university and career are personal (MU).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Pursuit of a music career and an openly gay relationship (Wikipedia; MU).

folkways.japan: Entrance exams to Kyoto University and graduation as a life turning point reflect Japanese school culture; the story stands somewhat apart from much BL convention (Wikipedia).

delivery.evidence: ANN calls the romance a 'quiet progression'; Comics Beat (via Wikipedia) a 'straightforward teenage romance' rather than message drama.

personified.ideology: an older gay man's experience and advice

delivery.note: Acceptance is shown through ordinary scenes rather than argued, and no character is set up to voice opposition.

winners_losers: The couple stays together across distance; no one is punished. Sympathy goes to young love and self-acceptance.
